stem.text: The depth of snow on a field, measured in inches, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function D of time t, measured in hours. It is known that \( D''(4) = -2.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( D''(4) = -2.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 4 hours, the rate at which the depth of snow on the field is changing is decreasing at a rate of 2.5 inches per hour per hour.

worked_solution.text: \( D''(4) \) is the rate of change of \( D' \), the rate at which the depth of snow on the field changes, so it is measured in inches per hour per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative as the rate of change of a rate

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at t = 4 the rate of change of the depth of snow on the field is itself decreasing, by 2.5 inches per hour for each hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the second derivative gives the direction of change of the rate
